entry.title: The Covering Radius of $\text{RM}(1,9)$ is Precisely $242$
entry.summary:
Let $\text{RM}(r,n)$ be the $r$th order Reed-Muller code of length $2^n$, and let $\rho(r,n)$ denote its covering radius, so that $\rho(1,n)$ is the largest possible nonlinearity of a Boolean function in $n$ variables. For odd $n$, the value of $\rho(1,n)$ was previously known only for $n\le 7$. It is known that $242\le\rho(1,9)\le 244$, but the exact determination of $\rho(1,9)$ has been a long-standing open question.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Optimal Threshold Implementations of all bijective 4-bit S-boxes and new Infinite Families
entry.summary:
Threshold implementations (TIs) are now an established class of side-channel countermeasures. Their underlying idea is simple and compelling: under mild, practical assumptions, they provide protection against glitches and allow composability. Yet our understanding of one-stage TIs with a minimal number of shares remains limited, both for cryptographically relevant families—particularly power functions—and for concrete small functions.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: On the (In)stability of Adaptive Fee Mechanisms in Multi-Chain Systems
entry.summary:
EIP-1559 has become the dominant transaction fee mechanism in permissionless blockchains, regulating scarce block space through an adaptive base fee. The design balances a trade-off between responsiveness to demand fluctuations and stability of long-term resource usage. On a single chain, this trade-off is well understood and empirically stable.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #cryptography #consensus

entry.title: ECHO: Replacing the Compliance Proxy with Response Harmfulness in Optimization-Based Jailbreak Attack
entry.summary:
Despite extensive safety alignment, large language models remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks. Existing optimization-based attacks share a single objective: maximize a token-level proxy of victim compliance---such as the likelihood of an affirmative prefix---computed on the prompt rather than the decoded reply. This proxy cannot distinguish a cautious hedge from a fully actionable harmful answer, leaving the search blind to what the model actually says.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #llm

entry.title: SAFE-Mem: Secure Agentic Memory with Fine-Grained Authority and Governance-Aware Retrieval
entry.summary:
Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on persistent memory to support long-term reasoning and personalized interactions. However, information collected from external sources can introduce security risks when untrusted claims (i.e., atomic statements) are later treated as authorized preferences, policies, or permissions. Existing defenses typically rely on content-based filtering or coarse-grained provenance tracking, which either fail to prevent unauthorized memory use or block legitimate information, sacrificing memory utility.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #llm #rust

entry.title: SCMAC and LOL2.0: An AEAD Design Framework and A New Version of LOL Stream Cipher Design Framework
entry.summary:
In this paper, we introduce SCMAC, a general framework that transforms large-memory stream ciphers into AEAD schemes. It represents an intermediate design paradigm between Encrypt-then-MAC and dedicated single-pass AEAD, partially integrating encryption and authentication mechanisms while mitigating the risk of state leakage associated with immediate absorption and squeezing. Consequently, this approach harmonizes high performance with enhanced security.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: SoK: Pseudorandom Generation for Masked Cryptographic Implementation. This paper investigates pseudorandom generation in the context of masked cryptographic implementation.
entry.summary:
This paper investigates pseudorandom generation in the context of masked cryptographic implementation. Although masking and pseudorandom generators (PRGs) have been distinctly studied for a long time, there has been little study on how randomness should be generated in masked implementation. The lack of analysis on mask-bits generators obscures the practical security of masked cryptographic implementation, potentially confusing practitioners (e.g., designer, implementer, and evaluator) about how to realize them securely.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics
